paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: A few months ago, I was down with a terrible cold which ended in a persistent bad cough. No matter how many different 26 I tried, I still couldn’t get rid of the cough. Not only did it 27 my teaching but also my life as a whole. Then one day after class, a student came up to me and 28 traditional Chinese medicine. From her description, Chinese medicine sounded as if it had magic power that worked wonders. I was 29 because I knew so little about it and have never it before. Eventually, my cough got so much 30 that I couldn’t sleep at night, so I decided to give it a try. The Chinese doctor took my pulse and asked to see my tongue, both of which were new 31 to me because they are both non-existent in Western medicine. Then the doctor gave me a scraping（刮）treatment known as “Gua Sha”. I was a little 32 at first because he used a smooth edged tool to scrape the skin on my neck and shoulders. A few minutes later, the 33 strokes started to produce a relieving effect and my body and mind began to 34 deeper into relaxation. I didn’t feel any improvement in my condition in the first couple of days, but after a few more regular visits to the doctor, my cough started to 35 . Then, within a matter of weeks, it was completely gone!
paragraphs.translationZh: 几个月前，我得了一场严重的感冒，最后导致了持续的剧烈咳嗽。不管我尝试了多少种偏方，还是无法摆脱咳嗽。这不仅给我的教学带来了不便，也给我的整个生活带来了不便。然后有一天下课后，一位学生向我推荐了中医。从她的描述中，中医听起来就像有神奇的力量。我很犹豫，因为我对它知之甚少，而且以前从未接触过。最终，我的咳嗽变得更加严重，以至于我晚上无法入睡，所以我决定尝试一下。中医给我把脉，让我看舌头，这对我来说都是新的体验，因为这都是西医中不存在的。然后医生给我进行了刮痧治疗，称为“刮痧”。起初我有点害怕，因为他用一个光滑边缘的工具刮我脖子和肩膀上的皮肤。几分钟后，压力开始产生缓解效果，我的身心开始更加放松。刚开始的几天，我并没有感觉自己的病情有任何好转，但经过几次定期去看医生后，我的咳嗽开始减轻了。然后，几周之内，它就完全消失了！

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: How a Poor, Abandoned Parisian Boy Became a Top Chef
paragraphs.translationZh: 一个贫穷、被遗弃的巴黎男孩如何成为顶级厨师

paragraphs.sourceText: A. When you drop a piece of food on the floor, is it really OK to eat if you pick it up within five seconds? An urban food myth contends that if food spends just a few seconds on the floor, dirt and germs won’t have much of a chance to contaminate it. Research in my lab has focused on how food becomes contaminated, and we’ve done some work on this particular piece of wisdom.
paragraphs.translationZh: A. 当你把一块食物掉在地上时，如果你在五秒钟之内捡起来，真的可以吃吗？一个城市食品神话认为，如果食物在地板上只停留几秒钟，污垢和细菌就没有太多机会污染它。我实验室的研究重点是食品如何被污染，我们已经针对这一特殊智慧做了一些工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. While the “five-second rule” might not seem like the most pressing issue for food scientists to get to the bottom of, it’s still worth investigating food myths like this one because they shape our beliefs about when food is safe to eat.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 虽然“五秒规则”似乎不是食品科学家需要弄清楚的最紧迫的问题，但仍然值得研究像这样的食品神话，因为它们塑造了我们对食品何时可以安全食用的信念。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. So is five seconds on the floor the critical threshold（门槛）that separates a piece of eatable food from a case of food poisoning? It’s a bit more complicated than that. It depends on just how many bacteria can make it from floor to food in a few seconds and just how dirty the floor is.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 那么，在地板上五秒是区分食物中毒与可食用食物的临界阈值吗？比这更复杂一点。这取决于几秒钟内有多少细菌可以从地板传播到食物，以及地板有多脏。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Wondering if food is still OK to eat after it’s dropped on the floor is a pretty common experience. And it’s probably not a new one either. A well-known, but inaccurate, story about Julia Child may have contributed to this food myth. Some viewers of her cooking show, The French Chef, insist they saw Child drop lamb on the floor and pick it up, with the advice that if they were alone in the kitchen, their guests would never know.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 想知道食物掉在地板上后是否还能吃是一种很常见的经历。而且它可能也不是新的。关于朱莉娅·柴尔德的一个众所周知但不准确的故事可能促成了这个食物神话。一些观看她的烹饪节目《法国厨师》的观众坚称，他们看到柴尔德把羊肉掉在地板上然后捡起来，并建议如果他们独自在厨房里，他们的客人永远不会知道。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. In fact it was a potato pancake, and it fell on the stovetop, not on the floor. Child put it back in the pan, saying, “But you can always pick it up and if you’re alone in the kitchen, who’s going to see it?” But the misremembered story persists. It’s harder to pin down the origins of the oft-quoted five-second rule, but a 2003 study reported that 70% of women and 56% of men surveyed were familiar with the five-second rule and that women were more likely than men to eat food that had dropped on the floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 事实上，这是一块土豆煎饼，它落在炉子上，而不是地板上。孩子把它放回锅里，说道：“但是你随时都可以把它捡起来，如果你一个人在厨房里，谁会看到它呢？”但这个被误记的故事仍然存在。确定经常被引用的五秒规则的起源比较困难，但 2003 年的一项研究报告称，接受调查的 70% 的女性和 56% 的男性熟悉五秒规则，并且女性比男性更有可能吃掉在地板上的食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. So what does science tell us about what a few moments on the floor means for the safety of your food? The earliest research report on the five-second rule is attributed to Jillian Clarke, a high school student participating in a research project at the University of Illinois. Clarke and her colleagues introduced bacteria to floor tiles（瓷砖）and then placed cookies on the tiles for varying times. They reported bacteria were transferred from the tiles to the cookies within five seconds, but didn’t report the specific amount of bacteria that made it from the tiles to the food.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 那么，关于在地板上呆一会儿对食品安全意味着什么，科学告诉我们什么呢？最早关于五秒钟规则的研究报告归功于伊利诺伊大学参与研究项目的高中生吉莉安·克拉克(Jillian Clarke)。克拉克和她的同事将细菌引入地砖，然后将饼干放在瓷砖上不同的时间。他们报告说细菌在五秒钟内从瓷砖转移到饼干上，但没有报告从瓷砖转移到食物中的细菌的具体数量。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. But how many bacteria actually transfer in five seconds? In 2007, my lab at Clemson University published a study in the Journal of Applied Microbiology. We wanted to know if the length of time food is in contact with a contaminated surface affected the rate of transfer of bacteria to the food. To find out, we introduced bacteria to squares of tile, carpet or wood. Five minutes after that, we placed either bacon or bread on the surface for 5,30 or 60 seconds, and then measured the number of bacteria transferred to the food. We repeated this exact procedure after the bacteria had been on the surface for 2,4,8 and 24 hours.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 但是五秒钟内实际上有多少细菌转移呢？ 2007 年，我在克莱姆森大学的实验室在《应用微生物学杂志》上发表了一项研究。我们想知道食品与受污染表面接触的时间长短是否会影响细菌转移到食品的速度。为了找到答案，我们将细菌引入方块瓷砖、地毯或木头中。五分钟后，我们将培根或面包放在表面 5,30 或 60 秒，然后测量转移到食物上的细菌数量。当细菌在表面停留 2、4、8 和 24 小时后，我们重复了这个精确的过程。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. We found that the number of bacteria transferred to either kind of food didn’t depend much on how long the food was in contact with the contaminated surface—whether for a few seconds or for a whole minute. The overall number of bacteria on the surface mattered more, and this decreased over time after the initial introduction. It looks like what’s at issue is less how long your food stays on the floor and much more how contaminated with bacteria that patch of floor happens to be.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 我们发现转移到任何一种食物中的细菌数量并不太取决于食物与受污染表面接触的时间——无论是几秒钟还是一整分钟。表面上的细菌总数更重要，并且在最初引入后随着时间的推移而减少。看起来问题不在于食物在地板上停留的时间，而在于这块地板被细菌污染的程度。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. We also found that the kind of surface made a difference as well. Carpets, for instance, seem to be slightly better places to drop your food than wood or tile. When a carpet was contaminated, less than 1% of the bacteria were transferred. But when the food was in contact with tile or wood, 45-70% of bacteria were.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 我们还发现表面的类型也会产生影响。例如，地毯似乎比木头或瓷砖更适合放置食物。当地毯被污染时，只有不到 1% 的细菌被转移。但当食物与瓷砖或木头接触时，45-70% 的细菌会存在。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. Last year, a study from Aston University in the UK used nearly identical parameters（参数）to our study and found similar results. They also reported that 87% of people asked either would eat or had eaten food fallen on the floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 去年，英国阿斯顿大学的一项研究使用了与我们的研究几乎相同的参数，并发现了相似的结果。他们还报告称，87% 的受访者要么会吃东西，要么吃过掉在地板上的食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Should you eat food fallen on the floor then? From a food safety standpoint, if you have millions or more bacteria on a surface, 0.1% is still enough to make you sick. Also, certain types of bacteria are extremely harmful, and it takes only a small number to make you sick. For example, 10 bacteria or less of an especially deadly strain of bacteria can cause severe illness and death in people with compromised immune systems. But the chance of these bacteria being on most surfaces is very low.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 那么你应该吃掉在地板上的食物吗？从食品安全的角度来看，如果表面有数百万或更多的细菌，0.1% 仍然足以让你生病。此外，某些类型的细菌极其有害，只需少量即可使您生病。例如，10 个或更少的特别致命的细菌菌株可能会导致免疫系统受损的人患上严重疾病甚至死亡。但这些细菌出现在大多数表面的机会非常低。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. And it’s not just dropping food on the floor that can lead to bacterial contamination. Bacteria are carried by various “media”, which can include raw food, moist surfaces where bacteria have been left, our hands or skin and from coughing or sneezing（打喷嚏）. Hands, foods and utensils（器皿）can carry individual bacteria living in communities contained within a protective film. These microscopic layers of deposits containing bacteria are known as biofilms and they are found on most surfaces and objects. Biofilm communities can harbor bacteria longer and are very difficult to clean. Becteria in these communities also have an enhanced resistance to sanitizers（清洁剂）and antibiotics compared to bacteria living on their own.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 不仅仅是食物掉在地板上会导致细菌污染。细菌通过各种“介质”携带，包括生食、残留有细菌的潮湿表面、我们的手或皮肤以及咳嗽或打喷嚏（打喷嚏）。手、食物和器皿可以携带生活在保护膜内群落中的单个细菌。这些含有细菌的微观沉积物层被称为生物膜，它们存在于大多数表面和物体上。生物膜群落可以更长时间地藏匿细菌，并且非常难以清洁。与单独生活的细菌相比，这些社区中的细菌对消毒剂和抗生素的抵抗力也增强。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. So the next time you consider eating fallen food, the odds are in your favor that you can eat it without getting sick. But in the rare chance that there is a micro-organism that there is a micro-organism that can make you sick on the exact spot where the food dropped, you can be fairly sure that the bug is on the food you are about to put in your mouth.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 所以，下次你考虑吃掉落的食物时，你吃掉它而不会生病的可能性对你有利。但在极少数的情况下，如果食物掉落的地方有一种微生物可以让你生病，那么你可以相当肯定，这种细菌就存在于你即将放入口中的食物上。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Research or common sense tells us that the best thing to do is keep your hands, utensils and other surfaces clean.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 研究或常识告诉我们，最好的办法是保持双手、器具和其他表面清洁。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. A research project found bacteria made their way to the food on the floor in five seconds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 一项研究项目发现，细菌在五秒钟内就到达了地板上的食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Whether food is contaminated depends much on the number of bacteria that get onto it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 食物是否受到污染很大程度上取决于食物上的细菌数量。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Food contamination may result from various factors other than food dropping on the floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 除了食物掉落在地板上之外，食物污染还可能由多种因素造成。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Males are less likely than females to eat food that may have been contaminated.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 男性比女性更不可能吃可能被污染的食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The author’s research centers around how food gets contaminated.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 作者的研究重点是食品如何被污染。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Keeping everything clean is the best way to stay healthy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 保持一切清洁是保持健康的最好方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Chances are you will not fall sick because of eating food picked up from the floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 你很可能不会因为吃了从地板上捡起的食物而生病。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. For a long time people have had the experience of deciding whether or not to eat food picked up from the floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 长期以来，人们都有决定是否吃从地板上捡起的食物的经验。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Some strains of bacteria are so harmful that a tiny few can have deadly consequences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 某些细菌菌株危害极大，极少数就可能造成致命后果。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Researchers found how many bacteria got onto the food did not have much to do with how long the food stayed on a contaminated floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 研究人员发现，食物上的细菌数量与食物在受污染地板上停留的时间没有太大关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 and 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 46 和 50 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The latest in cat research reveals that the lovely animal seems to have a basic grasp on both the laws of physics and the ins and outs of cause and effect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最新的猫研究表明，这种可爱的动物似乎对物理定律和因果关系的来龙去脉都有基本的掌握。

paragraphs.sourceText: According to a newly published study, cats seem to be able to predict the location of hiding prey（猎物）using both their ears and an inborn（天生的）understanding of how the physical world works.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据一项新发表的研究，猫似乎能够利用耳朵和对物质世界运作方式的天生理解来预测隐藏猎物的位置。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a recent experiment, Japanese researchers taped 30 domestic cats reacting to a container that a team member shook. Some containers rattled（发出响声）；others did not. When the container was tipped over, sometimes an object fell out and sometimes it didn’t.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在最近的一项实验中，日本研究人员记录了 30 只家猫对团队成员摇动的容器的反应。有些容器发出响声；有些则没有。当容器翻倒时，有时有物体掉出来，有时却没有。

paragraphs.sourceText: It turns out that the cats were remarkably smart about what would happen when a container was tipped over. When an object did not drop out of the bottom of a rattling container, they looked at it for a longer time than they did when the container behaved as expected.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实证明，猫对于容器翻倒时会发生的情况非常聪明。当一个物体没有从发出嘎嘎声的容器底部掉出来时，他们观察它的时间比容器按预期运行时观察的时间更长。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Cats use a causal-logical understanding of noise or sounds to predict the appearance of invisible objects,” lead researcher Saho Takagi says in a press release. The researchers conclude that cats’ hunting style may have developed based on their common-sense abilities to infer where prey is, using their hearing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 首席研究员 Saho Takagi 在一份新闻稿中表示：“猫利用对噪音或声音的因果逻辑理解来预测不可见物体的出现。”研究人员得出的结论是，猫的狩猎风格可能是基于它们利用听觉推断猎物所在位置的常识能力而发展起来的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Scientists have explored this idea with other endearing creatures: babies. Like cats, babies appear to engage in what’s called “preferential looking”—looking longer at things that are interesting or unusual than things they perceive as normal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学家们用其他可爱的生物：婴儿探索了这个想法。像猫一样，婴儿似乎会进行所谓的“优先观看”——对有趣或不寻常的事物的观察时间比对他们认为正常的事物的观察时间长。

paragraphs.sourceText: When babies’ expectations are violated in experiments like the ones performed with the cats, they react much like their animal friends. Psychologists have shown that babies apparently expect their world to comply with the laws of physics and cause and effect as early as two months of age.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当婴儿的期望在像对猫进行的实验中被违反时，他们的反应就像他们的动物朋友一样。心理学家表明，婴儿在两个月大时就显然希望他们的世界遵守物理定律和因果关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: Does the study mean that cats will soon grasp the ins and outs of cause and effect? Maybe. Okay, so cats may not be the next physics faculty members at America’s most important research universities. But by demonstrating their common sense, they’ve shown that the divide between cats and humans may not be that great after all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项研究是否意味着猫很快就能掌握因果关系的来龙去脉？或许。好吧，所以猫可能不会成为美国最重要的研究型大学的下一个物理教员。但通过展示他们的常识，他们表明猫和人类之间的鸿沟可能并没有那么大。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46.What do we learn from a newly published study about cats?
paragraphs.translationZh: 46.我们从一项新发表的关于猫的研究中学到了什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. What may account for the cats’ response to the noise from the containers?
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 什么可以解释猫对容器发出的噪音的反应？

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. What is characteristic of the way cats hunt, according to the Japanese researchers?
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 日本研究人员认为，猫的捕猎方式有何特点？

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. In what way do babies behave like cats?
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 婴儿在哪些方面表现得像猫？

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. What can we conclude about cats from the passage?
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 从这篇文章中我们可以得出关于猫的什么结论？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Imagine you enter a car with no steering wheel, no brake or accelerator padals（踏板）. Under a voice-activated command, you say an address. “The fastest route will take us 15.3 minutes. Should I take it?” You say “yes” and you are on your way. The car responds and starts moving all by itself. All you have to do is sit back and relax.
paragraphs.translationZh: 想象一下你进入一辆没有方向盘、没有刹车或油门踏板的汽车。在声控命令下，您说出一个地址。 “最快的路线需要15.3分钟。我应该走吗？”你说“是”，你就上路了。汽车做出响应并开始自行移动。您所要做的就是坐下来放松。

paragraphs.sourceText: How weird would it be if, one day in the future, everyone had such a car? No crazy driving, no insults, no cutting in; traffic laws would be respected and driving much safer. On the other hand, imagine the cost savings for local police enforcement and town budgets without all those speeding and parking tickets.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果有一天，每个人都拥有一辆这样的车，那该有多奇怪？不疯狂驾驶、不辱骂、不插队；交通法规将受到尊重，驾驶也会更加安全。另一方面，想象一下如果没有那些超速和停车罚单，当地警察执法和城镇预算将节省多少成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: A new technology has the potential to change modern society in radical ways. There’s no question that self-driving vehicles could be an enormous benefit. The potential for safer cars means accident statistics would drop: some 94% of road accidents in the U.S. involve human error. Older drivers and visually-or physically-impaired people would gain a new level of freedom. Maintaining safe speeds and being electric, self-driving cars would drastically reduce pollution levels and dependency on non-renewable fuels. Roads would be quieter, people safer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 新技术有可能从根本上改变现代社会。毫无疑问，自动驾驶汽车可以带来巨大的好处。更安全的汽车的潜力意味着事故统计数据将会下降：美国约 94% 的道路事故都涉及人为错误。年长的司机和视力或身体有障碍的人将获得新的自由度。保持安全速度和电动自动驾驶汽车将大大降低污染水平和对不可再生燃料的依赖。道路会更安静，人们会更安全。

paragraphs.sourceText: But we must also consider the impact of the new technology on those who now depend on driving for their livelihoods. According to the U.S. Department of Labor, in May 2015 there were 505,560 registered school bus drivers. The American Trucking Association lists approximately 3.5 million professional truck drivers in the U.S.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但我们还必须考虑新技术对那些现在依靠驾驶为生的人的影响。根据美国劳工部的数据，2015 年 5 月，有 505,560 名注册校车司机。美国卡车运输协会列出了美国大约 350 万专业卡车司机。

paragraphs.sourceText: The companies developing self-driving vehicles should be partnering with state and federal authorities to offer retraining for this massive workforce, many of whom will be displaced by the new technology. This is similar to what’s happening in the coal and oil industries, a situation that fuels much of the current political discontent in this country.
paragraphs.translationZh: 开发自动驾驶汽车的公司应该与州和联邦当局合作，为大量劳动力提供再培训，其中许多人将因新技术而失业。这与煤炭和石油行业发生的情况类似，这种情况加剧了该国当前的政治不满情绪。

paragraphs.sourceText: New technologies will, and should, be developed. This is how society moves forward. However, progress can’t be one-sided. It is necessary for the companies and state agencies involved to consider the ethical consequences of these potential changes to build a better future for all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 新技术将会而且应该被开发。社会就是这样前进的。然而，进步不能是一面倒的。相关公司和国家机构有必要考虑这些潜在变化的道德后果，以便为所有人建设更美好的未来。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51.What would be the impact of the extensive use of driverless cars?
paragraphs.translationZh: 51.无人驾驶汽车的广泛使用会产生什么影响？

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. How would the elderly and the disabled benefit from driverless cars?
paragraphs.translationZh: 52.老年人和残疾人如何从无人驾驶汽车中受益？

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. What would be the negative impact of driverless cars?
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 无人驾驶汽车会带来哪些负面影响？

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. What is the result of the introduction of new technologies in energy industries?
paragraphs.translationZh: 54.能源行业引进新技术的结果是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. What does the author suggest businesses and the government do?
paragraphs.translationZh: 55.作者建议企业和政府做什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
